definition: A method for injecting information about token order into transformer models, which otherwise have no inherent sense of sequence position.
details: Because self-attention processes all tokens simultaneously and has no built-in notion of order, positional encodings (sinusoidal, learned, or rotary) are added to token embeddings to preserve sequence information.

explainer.lead: Positional encoding injects token-order information into transformers, which otherwise have no inherent sense of sequence position. It matters because without it, self-attention treats a sequence as an unordered set.

tiers.eli5: Like numbering the words on a page so you know which comes first, since the reader sees them all at once.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers add sinusoidal, learned, or rotary encodings to token embeddings before attention; a pitfall is choosing an encoding whose behaviour degrades beyond the lengths seen in training.
tiers.paperLevel: Self-attention processes all tokens simultaneously with no built-in order, so positional encodings are added to token embeddings to preserve sequence information; common forms are sinusoidal, learned, and rotary.

explainer.example: Before attention, each token embedding has a positional vector added so that the model can distinguish 'dog bites man' from 'man bites dog'.
